program_overview.title: Alpha Girls
program_overview.tagline: The deepest technical road: systems at scale, reliability as a discipline, and the strategy skills of engineers whole companies listen to.
program_overview.description:
Some engineers choose depth as the career: the people rooms go quiet for when architecture is on the table. Alpha Girls is that road, built for experienced women engineers: system design at genuine scale, data platforms, reliability engineering with SLOs and honest incident practice, platform thinking, ML systems in production, security and compliance leadership, and the technical strategy craft, roadmaps, build-versus-buy, architecture reviews, that turns depth into organizational influence.

The course runs on artifacts: every month produces designs, reviews and documents of the kind staff and principal engineers are actually judged on, and it ends with the capstone, a complete system redesign proposal defended before a hard panel. No fantasy titles and no throne metaphors: scale is an engineering property here, not a personality.

Nine months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final defense that decides the certificate with a free retest. Depth, chosen deliberately.
what_makes_this_different: Scale as engineering, not vocabulary: capacity math, failure domains and cost curves done honestly
Reliability as a discipline: SLOs, incident command and postmortems practiced, not described
ML systems in production: the operational reality behind the model
Strategy as craft: roadmaps, reviews and build-vs-buy argued with artifacts
A senior peer room of women, rare and deliberately built
Real assessment: artifact reviews monthly and a final panel defense that decides the certificate, with a free retest

faqs.question: What is Alpha Girls, and who is it for?
faqs.answer: The deepest technical course in our women-in-tech ladder: systems at scale, reliability engineering, platforms, ML in production and technical strategy, for experienced women engineers (roughly 4+ years or Queen Coders graduates). It runs on staff-level artifacts, designs, ADRs, strategies, migration plans, and ends with a system redesign proposal defended before a panel.

faqs.question: How is this different from Queen Coders?
faqs.answer: Queen builds the step from good developer to trusted engineer: advanced engineering, AI fluency and first technical leadership. Alpha assumes that step and goes deeper into the senior IC road: scale, reliability, platforms and strategy, the work of staff and principal engineers. Many students take them in sequence with working years between.

faqs.question: Is this a management course?
faqs.answer: No: it is the senior individual-contributor road, walked deliberately. Leadership here means technical direction, reviews, mentoring and incident command, influence without the org chart. The management fork is examined honestly in Queen Coders; Alpha is for women who choose depth.

faqs.question: How is progress assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Homework follows every class, each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics, every phase closes with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: What does the final defense involve?
faqs.answer: A complete redesign proposal for a real system under real pressure: current-state honesty, target architecture with capacity and cost math, reliability and migration woven in, red-teamed by peers in week 35 and then defended before a panel that asks the questions real review boards ask. Passing it, plus the written paper, earns the certificate.
